explanations.explanation: Yes, fought is the word. Joshua tells them, “…it was the LORD your God who fought for you.” (Joshua 23:3) Later he says, “One of you can put a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God fights for you…” (Joshua 23:10) Joshua points them to the LORD as the one fighting for them, so he's the one to thank.

Close, because Joshua does say they saw everything the LORD did. But what he says the LORD did is fight for them. “…it was the LORD your God who fought for you.” (Joshua 23:3) Watching is my job when a batch is in the oven, and I'll be honest, I'm not even good at that.

Waiting sounds peaceful, but that's not the word Joshua uses. He says the LORD their God fought for them. “…it was the LORD your God who fought for you.” (Joshua 23:3) Waiting is something I know plenty about from my drawer years, and nobody ever won a thing doing it back there.

Yes, drive is the word. Joshua says the LORD their God will push those nations out of Israel's way and drive them out before them. The LORD is the one doing the driving here. Israel doesn't have to do it alone.

That's it, baker! The LORD drives the nations out so Israel can take possession of their land, and Joshua says it's “…as the LORD your God promised you.” (Joshua 23:5) Driving out, taking over and a promise, all packed into one verse. That's a well-packed cookie box.

Sharing is lovely when it's the last cookie in the box, but it's not what Joshua says here. He says the LORD will drive those nations out so Israel can take possession of their land. Same land, but a very different plan than splitting it.

Joshua doesn't have the nations packing up and leaving on their own. He says the LORD their God will push them out of Israel's way and drive them out. That's a lot more active than a polite wave goodbye. The LORD is doing the work.

Rebuilding is a good word, but it isn't in this verse. Joshua says the LORD will push those nations out and drive them out so Israel can take possession of their land (Joshua 23:5). The word for the blank is possess. Joshua says nothing here about what Israel will build. I'd love to rebuild my bakery too, but that's me talking, not Joshua.

explanations.answer: Keep all that's written in the Law of Moses
explanations.explanation: Yes, that's the reason for the strength. Joshua says, “Be very strong, then, so that you can keep and obey all that is written in the Book of the Law of Moses…” (Joshua 23:6) He's talking about holding onto what God has already said. Strong here means steady, not just muscles.

explanations.answer: Drive out every nation all by themselves
explanations.explanation: Joshua actually says the opposite. The LORD is the one who will push those nations out of Israel's way and drive them out (Joshua 23:5). And Joshua says the LORD fights for them (Joshua 23:10). The strength he asks for in verse 6 is for keeping and obeying what's written in the Book of the Law of Moses.

explanations.answer: Build a great temple for the LORD
explanations.explanation: No temple comes up in this speech at all. Joshua says to be very strong so they can keep and obey all that is written in the Book of the Law of Moses. That's the job he puts in front of them. I love a big building project, but this isn't one.

Joshua doesn't hand out a percentage. He says to keep and obey all that is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, “…not turning aside from it to the right or to the left.” (Joshua 23:6) No turning even a little. If I only followed most of a recipe, you'd taste it right away.

Right, and Joshua leaves no room for "mostly." He tells them to keep and obey all that is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, “…not turning aside from it to the right or to the left.” (Joshua 23:6) Not a little to either side. That's the whole charge.

Joshua says it plainly: “You must not call on the names of their gods or swear by them, and you must not serve them or bow down to them.” (Joshua 23:7) Swearing by a god means leaning on that god's name. Joshua closes that door along with calling on the name, serving and bowing.

Joshua actually says they must not. His words are “You must not call on the names of their gods or swear by them, and you must not serve them or bow down to them.” (Joshua 23:7) So swearing by those gods is off the table, right along with serving them and bowing down. He lists them out one by one.

That's it. Joshua says, “…you shall hold fast to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.” (Joshua 23:8) Notice the "…as you have done to this day." He's telling them to keep doing what they've been doing.

Joshua is the one talking, and he's pointing past himself. In this very speech he says, “…today I am going the way of all the earth…” (Joshua 23:14) The elders are in the room, but he tells Israel to hold fast to the LORD their God. That's who they're to hold onto.

Eleazar doesn't show up anywhere in this speech. Joshua names who to hold fast to: “…the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.” (Joshua 23:8) The name sounds official, so it's an easy one to grab. But the text keeps it simple, and the answer is the LORD.

Yes, a thousand. Joshua says, “One of you can put a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God fights for you, just as He promised.” (Joshua 23:10) Look at the reason he gives: the LORD fights for them. One Israelite doesn't do this alone.

A hundred is a nice round number, but Joshua goes bigger. He says one of them can put a thousand to flight. And he gives the reason right away: the LORD their God fights for them, just as He promised (Joshua 23:10).

Ten thousand is a big swing, baker, and I respect it. But Joshua's number is a thousand. “One of you can put a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God fights for you, just as He promised.” (Joshua 23:10) I only stretch numbers in my own jokes, and Joshua doesn't need my help.

explanations.answer: That they love the LORD their God
explanations.explanation: That's the one. Joshua says, “Therefore watch yourselves carefully, that you love the LORD your God.” (Joshua 23:11) After all that talk of battles and land, the thing he wants guarded is their love for the LORD.

explanations.answer: That their borders stay well guarded
explanations.explanation: Borders sound sensible, but that's not what Joshua says to watch. He says, “Therefore watch yourselves carefully, that you love the LORD your God.” (Joshua 23:11) The watching is aimed at themselves, not at a fence. I'll admit a fence is easier to inspect than a heart.

explanations.answer: That their armies stay ready to fight
explanations.explanation: You'd think an old leader would say that, but Joshua doesn't. His words are “Therefore watch yourselves carefully, that you love the LORD your God.” (Joshua 23:11) The watching is about love. A few verses earlier he's already said the LORD is the one who fights for them.

Joshua says the opposite. If they turn away and cling to those nations, he says, “…the LORD your God will no longer drive out these nations before you.” (Joshua 23:13) The driving out is tied to how Israel lives. It doesn't keep going no matter what.
Right. Joshua says, “…the LORD your God will no longer drive out these nations before you.” (Joshua 23:13) That's what happens if they turn away and cling to those nations. The driving out stops.

explanations.answer: Something that traps and hurts them
explanations.explanation: Yes. Joshua says those nations will become “…a snare and a trap, a scourge in your sides and thorns in your eyes…” (Joshua 23:13) A snare and a trap catch you, and a scourge and thorns hurt. That's four pictures in one verse, and not one of them is comfortable.

That's the opposite of what Joshua warns. He says those nations will become “…a snare and a trap, a scourge in your sides and thorns in your eyes…” (Joshua 23:13) None of those pictures is a buddy at your side. Thorns in your eyes aren't a team.

Joshua doesn't paint it that way. He says they will become “…a snare and a trap, a scourge in your sides and thorns in your eyes…” (Joshua 23:13) Nobody is working a field in that picture. It's all traps and thorns.

Joshua says not one has failed. His words are “…not one of the good promises the LORD your God made to you has failed. Everything was fulfilled for you; not one promise has failed.” (Joshua 23:14) He says it twice, and he says they know it with all their heart and soul.

Yes, the answer is False. Joshua says, “…not one of the good promises the LORD your God made to you has failed. Everything was fulfilled for you; not one promise has failed.” (Joshua 23:14) He says it two ways, back to back. He also says they know it with all their heart and soul.

Joshua says both halves. “…just as every good thing the LORD your God promised you has come to pass, likewise the LORD will bring upon you the calamity He has threatened…” (Joshua 23:15) I think this is a heavy verse. The good promises came to pass, and Joshua says the threatened calamity will too.

Joshua really does say both. “…just as every good thing the LORD your God promised you has come to pass, likewise the LORD will bring upon you the calamity He has threatened…” (Joshua 23:15) It's a heavy thing to hear, and I think he knows it. The good promises came true, and so will the threat.

explanations.answer: Breaking His covenant and serving other gods
explanations.explanation: That's what Joshua says. “If you transgress the covenant of the LORD your God, which He commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them, then the anger of the LORD will burn against you…” (Joshua 23:16) It's a serious verse. The cause is named plainly: breaking the covenant, serving other gods and bowing down to them.

explanations.answer: Losing a battle to the nations around them
explanations.explanation: Joshua doesn't name a lost battle. He says the anger of the LORD will burn if they “…transgress the covenant of the LORD your God…” and go serve other gods and bow down to them (Joshua 23:16). The cause is turning away from the covenant.

explanations.answer: Leaving the land to go live somewhere else
explanations.explanation: Moving isn't what Joshua points to. He says the anger of the LORD will burn if they “…transgress the covenant of the LORD your God, which He commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them…” (Joshua 23:16) The land comes up in the warning, but the cause is serving other gods.
